findings.issue: だった is the plain past of だ; the past of です is でした. Calling だった a 'form of です' contradicts the token note ('past stem of だ') and standard teaching.

notes: Past of です is でした; だった is the plain past of だ. Contradicts the record's own token note ('past stem of だ') and teaches the wrong paradigm. Suggested fix is good.
Genki-style pedagogy standardly presents だ/だった as the casual (short) forms of です; 'simple past (casual) form of です' is defensible shorthand, and '(casual)' rules out confusion with でした.

findings.issue: どうも is a single indivisible adverb but is tokenized as どう + も, implying the も is the particle も. どう alone means 'how', not 'thanks'; the gloss/role placed on どう is false, and en ('thanks, cheers') vs pt ('muito, valeu') glosses are inconsistent.
findings.current: advérbio (interjeição de agradecimento)
findings.suggested: Merge どう+も into one token どうも, gloss 'thanks (casual)' / 'valeu, obrigado'; も here is not the particle も.
findings.fix: Merge どう+も into one token どうも, gloss 'thanks (casual)' / 'valeu, obrigado'; も here is not the particle も.
notes: どうも is one lexeme (UniDic treats it as a single adverb). どう alone means 'how' — glossing it 'thanks, cheers' is factually false, and bare も invites misreading as the additive particle. Unlike そんな+に, the parts don't carry the meaning. Merge is correct.
どうも is one indivisible word; split as どう+も the null-glossed も reads as the particle, and どう alone means 'how', making the 'thanks' gloss on どう false. Merge into a single どうも token.

findings.issue: Generated JP is unnatural: comma splice joining a plain predicate (正しい) to a polite one (です) in one sentence, and the concessive 尤も normally starts a new clause/sentence with the caveat ending in が. The expl's claim that this mix is 'common' papers over the defect.

findings.issue: その is described as 'far from the speaker', which is the description of あの (far from both speaker and listener). その marks something near the listener or already mentioned in the discourse (anaphoric, the sense used here). Teaches the ko-so-a-do system incorrectly.

'Far from the speaker' is あの's description; その is near-listener/anaphoric (anaphoric here). Misteaches ko-so-a-do in a demonstrative gloss.

notes: 'As for' is this corpus's は-topic device (used for は in 6 sibling sentences); 作品を is a を object per the record's own expl. Misteaches the particle.
Every other 'As for' in this batch maps to は; using it for を-marked 作品 contradicts the expl and teaches を as topic.

findings.issue: 何億 (なんおく) is romanized 'nanoku', which reads as な-の-く. Syllabic ん before a vowel requires an apostrophe in Hepburn: nan'oku.

Systemic convention, not a per-sentence defect: no sentence romaji in the corpus uses n' (teninsan, takusanaru, ichimanen). Needs a corpus-wide romanizer policy fix, like the punctuation issue.

findings.issue: 点いか (てんいか) is romanized 'tenika', which reads as て-に-か. Syllabic ん before a vowel requires an apostrophe: ten'ika.

Same systemic apostrophe-less romanizer convention across the entire sentence bank; fixing one sentence would create inconsistency. Duplicate of the corpus-wide issue.

findings.issue: 'Fora aos domingos' is nonstandard: the exceptive 'fora' takes the noun phrase directly ('fora os domingos'); combining it with the contracted adverbial 'aos' is awkward pt-BR.

Exceptives take adverbial PPs in pt-BR ('exceto/menos aos domingos' are standard); 'fora aos domingos' parses the same way and is acceptable colloquial pt-BR. Stylistic preference only.

あの人 is が-marked; expl correctly calls it subject/target of the emotive adjective. Applying the は-mirror 'Quanto a' in lit_pt contradicts the record's own explanation and blurs the は/が contrast.

findings.issue: 電車 is marked by が (subject), not topic は, yet the literal uses the topic device 'Quanto ao' (and lit_en uses 'As for the train'). This teaches が as if it were は; the expl correctly calls 電車が the subject.

電車が is subject (expl says so); 'Quanto ao trem' wrongly applies the は topic device. lit_en 'As for the train' has the same defect and should be fixed in the same pass (e.g. 'The train (subject) stopped smoothly at the platform.').

findings.issue: 温かい means 'warm', not 'hot' (that is 熱い). The token gloss says '(was) warm, lukewarm' and en says 'really warm'; 'very hot' in the literal field misteaches the 温かい/熱い contrast.

温かい is 'warm' (熱い is 'hot'); lit_en 'very hot' contradicts the record's own en ('really warm') and token gloss '(was) warm, lukewarm', misteaching the 温かい/熱い contrast. 'very warm' is correct.

findings.issue: In また後で電話します, また means 'de novo' (again), as both natural translations render it; 'Também' shifts the sense to 'in addition (to something else)'. lit_en 'Also,' has the same problem and should read 'Again,'.

In また後で電話します, また unambiguously means 'again' (both natural translations render it 'de novo'/'again'); 'Também' picks the wrong sense and changes the proposition. lit_en 'Also,' should likewise become 'Again,'.

findings.issue: 授業の間 means 'during the class' (the duration of the class itself), not 'the class break'. 'Break' would be 休み時間/合間. Contradicts the (correct) expl_en, which says 間 marks the whole duration of the class.

間 in 授業の間 is the duration of the class itself; 'class break' means recess (休み時間) and contradicts the item's own correct expl_en about the target word.

Glossing 涼しい with 'frio' contradicts the item's own expl_pt (fresco, not frio) and the fresco/frio distinction being taught; but the proposed fix is redundant pt-BR.

findings.issue: Generated JP asserts a third person's desire with bare 〜たい (妹は…習いたい). Plain declarative たい is restricted to the speaker (or questions); third person requires たがっている or evidential marking — exactly the rule JLPT texts teach. As a standalone model sentence it teaches a wrong pattern.
findings.current: 妹はピアノを習いたい
findings.suggested: 妹はピアノを習いたがっている
findings.fix: Prefer 私はピアノを習いたい — keeps the たい teaching target that expl_en/expl_pt and the tokens are built around (only 妹→私 changes; update kana/romaji/en/pt/lit). 妹はピアノを習いたがっている is also grammatical but silently retargets the record to たがる, forcing a full rewrite of expl and tokens.
notes: Bare declarative たい is speaker-restricted; standalone 妹は…習いたい is the canonical error たがる exists to fix. gen=true, so no human-source defense.
Bare declarative 3rd-person たい violates the person restriction (たい vs たがる is core N4); as a gen=true model sentence it teaches the wrong pattern, and expl claims たい expresses the subject's desire.

findings.issue: Claims word order is 'always' place → object → verb. Japanese pre-verbal order is flexible: ポスターを壁に張る is equally grammatical and common. Teaching an absolute rule that does not exist misleads learners.
findings.current: The order is always place → object → verb.
findings.suggested: The most common order is place → object → verb, but the two can swap as long as the verb stays last.
findings.fix: The most common order is place → object → verb, but the two can swap as long as the verb stays last.
notes: 'Always' is a false absolute: ポスターを壁に張る is fully grammatical; only verb-final order is fixed in Japanese. Genuine pedagogy error.
Both 壁にポスターを張る and ポスターを壁に張る are grammatical; pre-verbal argument order is flexible. 'Always' teaches a nonexistent absolute rule. Suggested fix is sound.

findings.issue: Same false absolute rule as expl_en: 'sempre lugar → objeto → verbo'. Japanese allows ポスターを壁に張る; only the verb-final position is fixed.

notes: Same false absolute in pt-BR ('sempre'). Pre-verbal に/を phrases can swap; teaching 'sempre' misleads learners.
Same false absolute in pt-BR ('sempre lugar → objeto → verbo'); only verb-final position is fixed. Suggested fix is sound.

findings.issue: The literal mirror invents a topic ('As for the night') that does not exist in the Japanese: 夜に is the complement of なる inside the と-clause, not a は-topic. Misrepresents the structure the field is supposed to teach.

findings.suggested: When (it) becomes night, (it) turns cool.
findings.fix: When (it) becomes night, (it) turns cool.
notes: No は in 夜になると涼しくなる. Batch convention uses 'As for' only for は-topics; 夜に is the complement of なる. Invented topic breaks the structural mirror.
No は-topic exists; 夜に is the complement of なる inside the と-clause. Corpus convention reserves 'As for X' for は-topics (cf. 母は → 'As for the mother'), so the mirror misteaches structure.

findings.issue: Claims に 'indicates where the action happens' — that is で's function. With 書く, に marks the surface/target where the name ends up (point of arrival), a core に-vs-で distinction; as written it teaches the wrong particle rule.

notes: 'Where the action happens' is で's rule. With 書く, に marks the target surface where the name ends up. As written it teaches the wrong に-vs-で rule in a pedagogical explanation.
'Where the action happens' is で's textbook definition. With 書く, に marks the surface/target of the result (紙に vs 図書館で) — a core N5 contrast taught wrong here.
